title: Substitutions 3
alt: BREAKING: Channing Tatum and his friends explore haunted city
transcript:
[Caption above the panel:]
Even More
Substitutions
That make reading the news more fun

[A table of words/sentences on the left that change in to those on the left. Between each set of words there is an arrow pointing from right.]

Gaffe                	➜	Magic spell
Ancient              	➜	Haunted
Star-Studded         	➜	Blood-soaked
Remains to be seen   	➜	Will never be known
Silver bullet        	➜	Way to kill werewolves
Subway system        	➜	Tunnels I found
Surprising           	➜	Surprising (but not to me)
War of words         	➜	Interplanetary war
Tension              	➜	Sexual tension
Cautiously optimistic	➜	Delusional
Doctor Who           	➜	The Big Bang Theory
Win votes            	➜	Find Pokémon
Behind the headlines 	➜	Beyond the grave
Email \
Facebook Post        	➜	Poem
Tweet /
Facebook CEO         	➜	This guy
Latest               	➜	Final
Disrupt              	➜	Destroy
Meeting              	➜	Ménage à trois
Scientists           	➜	Channing Tatum and his friends
You won't believe    	➜	I'm really sad about
explanation:
This is the third comic in the Substitution series where Randall suggests substitutions that will make reading the news more fun. But there have been several comics using substitutions both before and after these ones. This is the full series:
*1288: Substitutions 
*1625: Substitutions 2
*1679: Substitutions 3

The title text in original form would be "Scientists explore ancient city", which most would consider a fairly bland headline. Two days before this comic came out, there was news that a potential ancient Mayan city had been found by a 15 year old boy through satellite imagery, which may be what Randall was referencing. The Mayan city has now been proven nonexistent. Imagining Channing Tatum and his "friends", and pretending that the city is haunted, provides a much more dramatic setting mirroring many episodes (and later films) of Scooby Doo featuring a gang of friends (Mysteries, Inc.).

===Table of Substitutions===

Original word/phrase 	Substitution              	Explanation
Gaffe                	Magic spell               	A Gaffe is a social mistake, or . A magic spell is a series of actions or words used to create an effect through magic. Possibly a comment on how seemingly random words or actions can have dramatic consequences.
Ancient              	Haunted                   	Old structures and objects in certain genres of fiction, particularly , are frequently haunted.
Star-studded         	Blood-soaked              	Star-studded means featuring a lot of popular celebrities. Blood-soaked means covered in blood, or can be used to describe a place where a lot of violent deaths occurred. This might suggest that concentrating famous people in one place is likely to lead to bloodshed. If you were studded with throwing stars you might be blood-soaked.
Remains to be seen   	Will never be known       	The first phrase means that something is not known, while the second phrase means that something cannot be known. This adds a layer of fantastical mystery to an otherwise mundane phrase.
Silver bullet        	Way to kill werewolves    	Replaces a phrase usually used for it's metaphorical meaning with the literal purpose the metaphor was derived from.
In  folklore, a  was usually the best way to kill a werewolf permanently, as most conventional methods would leave it able to recover. Thus the phrase "silver bullet" is metaphorically used to mean something like "perfect solution." In a more literal sense, this also means that silver bullets are indeed a "way to kill werewolves."
Subway system        	Tunnels I found           	A more personal and colloquial way to refer to underground tunnels, as though they had just been discovered for the first time.
Could also be some other kind of tunnels, such as a sewage system that the author uses for transport, which would be very strange.
Surprising           	Surprising (but not to me)	The speaker/writer claims that everyone else is surprised by something, but they had anticipated it all along.
War of words         	Interplanetary war        	A pun based on the original phrase's similarity to "War of Worlds," meaning interplanetary war, (a major conflict involving the civilizations of multiple planets), or it's similarity to War of the Worlds, a book about interplanetary war.
Tension              	Sexual tension            	Inserts a single word to make a situation way weirder. (Sexual tension is a situation in which two or more people attempt to avoid acknowledging being sexually attracted to each other.)
Cautiously optimistic	Delusional                	Replaces a cautious and moderate opinion with an extremely supportive one.
                     	                          	Replaces one popular TV series with another unrelated one.
Win votes            	Find                      	Pokémon is a game franchise based around trying to collect a complete set of characters. This substitution suggests that the vote hunter is on a quest to collect the votes (of outlandish creatures) one by one.
Behind the headlines 	Beyond the grave          	Essentially unrelated phrases that sound similar.
Email /  post /      	Poem                      	This substitution has some historical merit as poets often used their artform as a medium to spread their opinions to a large number of people.
Facebook CEO         	This guy                  	When the comic was released, the Facebook CEO was , meaning this phrase would usually appear in the form "this guy Mark Zuckerberg," implying Mark Zuckerberg isn't special or important, but rather just a random person who happened to say something.
Latest               	Final                     	This substitution means that any recent entry in a series will be treated as the final one. Possibly a joke about the ambiguity in the use of the word "last."
Disrupt              	Destroy                   	Replaces a fairly standard "" phrase with a much more violent one.
Meeting              	Ménage à trois            	Another entry that attempts to make the mundane weird. A meeting is a gathering of people to discuss a topic, as in business, while a ménage à trois is one or more sex acts performed among three people.
Scientists           	and his friends           	Replaces a vague, anonymous phrase for a group of people with a very specific yet almost certainly unrelated group of people, given the context.
Channing Tatum is a famous actor and was likely chosen at random.
You won't believe    	I'm really sad about      	Replaces a catchphrase used in "click-bait" headlines to attract attention and web traffic with a more sincere yet uncharacteristically personal phrase expressing genuine disappointment in the topic.
